industry.why: Neutral, carried unchanged by judgement; see component 1, Special topics, Topic 1 (Recruitment Services). Component 1 regime, 2-Oct-26 (rates-led late cycle, hiking path marked down for the first time this week, growth firm at the level and rolling at the margin, index calm with risk-off running beneath it through breadth, size and rate sensitivity, not through defensives; sources present 2026-W40): the industry's composite rank (66, from 20 on 3-Jul) is a relief rally in the artificial-intelligence-exposed labour-service names measured by a composite weighted to the last six months, with the twelve-month return still -6.94% against the index; the seven sectors are split (Recruitment D, Advertising C, Testing B, the rest C) and the sector rows carry the view. Relative strength C now, C prior. Counter-case: if the recruiters' rebound is the early-cycle hiring turn, this industry leads and C is late.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight; see component 1, Special topics, Topic 1 (Recruitment Services), which carries the same letter. Component 1 regime, 2-Oct-26 (rates-led late cycle, hiking path marked down for the first time this week, growth firm at the level and rolling at the margin, index calm with risk-off running beneath it through breadth, size and rate sensitivity, not through defensives; sources present 2026-W40): the sector rose with the same artificial-intelligence-fear reversal as the recruiters (WPP +56.6%, JCDecaux +27.9% from 1-Jul to 1-Oct) but its footing is firmer: twelve-month relative return +3.1%, rank 83 reached in July and held, sell-side momentum B for WPP and JCDecaux, and the 'first budget cut' case that set D has not appeared in the growth data (US GDP +3.4%, euro area expanding). Relative strength B now, C prior, agrees on direction. Counter-case: advertising is still the first discretionary corporate spend cut when the margin rolls over, and the consumer-agent theme threatens the brands that buy it; balanced, so Neutral.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for a view named and judged thin. Goldman (19 Oct) names the UK index among those rallying with non-AI, low-beta exposures; its UK Weekly Kickstart 'The Value of Earnings' and the podcast 'The cavalry isn't coming: UK stocks' were titles only; the Bank of England and gilt yields were not read. One clause of index leadership on a 191-stock row, the largest in the table, is not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to B if a second source makes the UK case with a rate path read.

memo.verdict: Bullish in direction; progress to an Early-Stage look rather than park; conviction low, a working hypothesis. Capital is not argued for at 378.6p (2026-10-12): the three-year 'Modal return' clears the 20 percent bar only below about 352p, 8 percent beneath the price, while the eighteen-month return clears it at any price up to about 414p. The park rule does not bite: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C. Two dated tests inside three months resolve the one condition that sets the multiple: the third-quarter 2026 trading update (late October 2026; invalidation test a like-for-like decline worse than -3.5%) and the Coca-Cola international media decision (by December 2026; $1.4bn of billings). A Coca-Cola loss plus a third quarter worse than -3.5% takes the odds on the condition to about a third, the blended multiple to about 6.3x (today's price, no return but the yield) and the case to park. The Early-Stage brief is narrow: the win-loss record in Media and Enterprise Solutions pitches against Publicis and Omnicom over the first half of 2026; the Enterprise Solutions growth rate ahead of its January 2027 disclosure; the incentive pool's path to 6 percent of staff costs.
case: 1. The change is internal, broad and resourced, and it is the case. Five of twelve internal forces are strong and dated within fourteen months against a screen rule of three: a chief executive from outside the industry with long-dated incentives and two open-market purchases; a new chair and a rebuilt leadership team; Elevate28 (26 February 2026) in three dated phases (Stabilise 2026; Build 2027 with a return to organic growth; Accelerate 2028 with margin expansion), £500m of gross savings by end-2028 funded by £400m of integration cash; a holding company collapsed into four units and one segment, 25 agencies into four, 1,400 legal entities removed; incentives split 50/50 group and unit with relative organic growth at 16.67% of the long-term plan; more than 15 disposals in the first half of 2026. False positives clear: not a caretaker, funded in cash, no crown jewels, the dividend halved rather than borrowed for. The two screen signals that fail, guidance not raised (D) and shareholder returns cut (F), fail because the base is being reset before it is raised.

2. The external forces run the other way and are already in the base. Market advertising grows 8.9% in 2026 and agencies capture about 1%; competition tightens against WPP specifically (sixteen quarters of share loss; win-to-loss 1.3 against 3.3; Publicis undercutting with bundle pricing; Omnicom-Interpublic); generative AI deflates time-based fees (75% of the business; creative about 35% of sales) and management expects near-term fee deflation; litigation is a headwind. Only the company's own cycle (B: from -6.9% in Q4 2025 to -2.8% in Q2 2026, with a 500 to 600 basis point account-loss drag dated to FY2026) and regulation (C: no forced Google AdX divestiture in September 2026; cookies kept) help. External forces D; Change Forces B overall because the self-help is the case.

3. The change has travelled four of six layers. People, choices and actions are in place; the operating metrics turned in Q2 2026 (-2.8% against -6.0%; margin held at 8.4%; first for net new business); the financial statements have not turned (FY2026 EPS falls about 16 percent to about 53p); the sell-side moved one notch (consensus FY2026 EPS +4.8% over three months, +6.7% over six, the first upgrades since 2022). 'Financial Outputs' C: sell-side upgrades B (likely over six to twelve months: consensus at the low end of the margin guidance; targets +22% over three months; Bernstein 'a prudent deceleration'; Redburn expecting consensus to the upper end; two Sells and a zero one-month revision keep it from A); key metrics C ('low but improving': revenue growth C, margin C, cash conversion C, net debt B); Goldilocks growth D (six months F, a fall; eighteen months C, +9% to +14% a year from the FY2026 trough; three years D, about 10% a year); staircase B (Q3 update; Coca-Cola by December 2026; FY2026 results 25 February 2027; a new chief financial officer; Enterprise Solutions disclosure from 1 January 2027; the first positive organic quarter during 2027; Kantar 1H27; Burson; the Creative succession; the £500m run-rate in 2028).
counter_case: WPP's stabilisation is a temporary cyclical bounce dressed by a cost holiday, and the structure keeps deteriorating beneath it: the 'false friend', selected by the risk research's analysis of competing hypotheses as the best supported of three. The first-half 2026 margin beat came from £51m less severance and an incentive pool at 1.2 percent of net sales, both reversing in the second half by up to 200 basis points. Q2's -2.8% was -3.8% underlying, flattered by a 2.9-point easier comparison and by 2026's World Cup and United States midterms. The growth gap to Publicis widened in the very quarter WPP stabilised (-2.8% against +4.8%) and has run sixteen quarters; the win-to-loss ratio of 1.3 against 3.3 says gross losses continue (IBM and Novo Nordisk went to Omnicom since August) and $3.5bn of billings are under review. Creative is about 35 percent of sales and AI deflates its time-based fees faster than any savings programme; the data model is leased while the market pays for owned data, which is why Publicis at 11x looks 'justified' to the sell-side. The chief financial officer resigned seven weeks after the results the research called a turning point, into Diageo, and the executive who knew the cash and restructuring numbers best chose to leave before Phase 2; the Creative chief executive follows in March 2027. The balance sheet at 2.2x cannot buy the capability Publicis bought (LiveRamp; EUR 300m for CoreAI). The previous two restructurings under two previous chief executives failed on the same promise; three restructurings under three chief executives since 2018 each failed to deliver sustainable organic growth or bridge the peer margin gap. The whistleblower suit, if any of it is proven, breaks the trust on which the media arm's margin rests, because that margin relies on non-disclosed principal buying. The rally is named in the industry reading as an AI-loser relief rebound to be separated from real recoveries. On that path FY2027 organic growth stays negative, the margin stalls at 12% to 13%, the multiple returns to 5.7x and then toward the 4x to 4.15x that the bear case and the five-year record both hold (249p at 4.15x on consensus earnings, -34 percent), and the three-year return is about 5 percent a year with dividends on the uncleared branch or negative at the trough multiple; the sell-side's bears hold this view (Goldman Sachs 275p, UBS 250p; Morgan Stanley's 70p bear case before coverage ended). The record concedes: the first-half margin quality is weak and the second-half step-down real; the Q2 rate overstates the run-rate by about a point; the data deficit is structural and the thesis does not fix it; the leadership gap is live; the base rate of WPP turnarounds is poor; the price has taken the easy half of the re-rating; and the entry is 8 percent above where the three-year return clears the bar. The record's response: the account-loss drag is arithmetic (500 to 600 basis points), not narrative, and dated to FY2026; both halves of the growth engine have turned (existing-client spend positive excluding losses; first by net billings for net new business); the counter-case names its own disconfirming tests (a positive organic quarter; a margin above 13 percent without severance holidays), both observable inside eighteen months; the entry multiple already prices the counter-case (6x discounts a 10 percent terminal revenue decline and 10 percent margins per Redburn), so the modal path need only be plausible for the odds to favour the long; and the downside on the uncleared branch is bounded by a 4.0 percent yield and a multiple at the two-year median. Where the counter-case wins: a Coca-Cola loss plus a Q3 worse than -3.5%, taking the odds on the condition to about a third and the blended multiple to about 6.3x, today's price. At Building Block level the record also carried: the 'Foundations' are a C because the structure is a three-player oligopoly with five-to-seven-year review cycles and WPP just won the most (held at D because the pull is toward data owners and every output misses threshold; would move to C on two quarters matching Publicis or a half-year win-to-loss above 2); the fit is a third restructuring of a serial disappointer, not a 'Major Corporate Change' (held because breadth, not originality, is the test, and two output series are unambiguous; would fall to C on a Q3 worse than -3.5% or an FY2026 margin below 12%); the 'Investment Case' is a C because the risks are a turnaround's ordinary furniture (held because one actual and four probable problems in two months is the specific invalidating pattern and nine concerns against three is not a near miss; would move to C on a Q3 at or better than -3.5%, Coca-Cola retained and a full-year margin at or above 12.5%).
triggers: - Q3 2026 trading update, late October 2026: like-for-like worse than -3.5% is the first invalidation test and the Alarm level on the first Key Driver; the comparison is 2.9 points harder than Q2.

- Coca-Cola international media review, decision by December 2026, $1.4bn of billings: retention plausible to probable (about 60 percent); a loss is about one point of net sales; a loss plus a Q3 worse than -3.5% invalidates (odds on the condition to about a third; blended multiple about 6.3x; case to park).

- FY2026 results, 25 February 2027: headline margin below 12% invalidates the margin Key Driver; FY2027 guidance holding the margin flat for a second year is the Alarm; a margin held only by severance holidays is the Alarm on the AI-deflation Key Risk; a chief financial officer not named by then is the Alarm on the finance succession, with disposals and savings slipping the Invalidate.
- FY2027 like-for-like negative at the February 2028 results invalidates the first Key Driver and sets the multiple on the uncleared branch (5.7x).

- Enterprise Solutions disclosed separately from 1 January 2027 (13% of net sales; growth unknown); Kantar consumer-data tranche in 1H27 (timing unconfirmed); Burson review outcome; Creative succession early 2027; the first positive organic quarter during 2027; the £500m run-rate and 16% to 17% margin ambition in 2028.

- Monitoring series: like-for-like net sales by quarter; top-25 client spend excluding losses; net new business and billings under review (COMvergence; $3.5bn under review); headline margin against the 12% floor; savings against £100m; staff incentives as a share of net sales (2.7% in H1 2026; 6% of staff costs the health marker); average net debt against £3.4bn (the risk research's re-run trigger); multiple against 5.7x on unchanged earnings; a cut of 2 percent or more to FY2027 consensus EPS; a further top-ten account loss; H2 2026 CPG budget cuts; Glassdoor senior-management score; WPP Open users.
